newsitem.title: UK: Most UK adverts for alcohol comply with code.
newsitem.headline: Most UK adverts for alcohol comply with code.

text.p: The vast majority of advertisements for alcoholic drinks in Britain are in line with advertising codes of conduct, an industry regulatory group said on Wednesday.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA), a self-regulatory body that oversees press and poster advertising, said a survey of 359 adverts for alcoholic drinks found that more than 98 percent were acceptable under the British codes of Advertising and Sales Promotion.

The ASA, which typically checks code compliance in the run-up to Christmas when alcohol advertising is heaviest, said only six of the 359 adverts surveyed were found to be unacceptable. Two adverts were found to be socially irresponsible becausae they portrayed excessive alcohol consumption.
One of the unacceptable ads showed a cartoon of a beer-bellied man with a line of bottles beside him. A second ad showed a number of inebriated characters coming out of a champagne bottle.
A third advert was found unacceptable because it showed a model who appeared to be under age 25 drinking beer.
The ASA said a fourth advert raised concerns under code rules prohibiting advertising from providing information on the alcoholic strength of a drink.

Although so-called alcopops, fruit-flavoured, carbonated alcoholic drinks, have been the source of concern, the ASA said none of the 12 adverts for alcopops included in its survey broke advertising codes.
